source_caption:
Before he became one of the most celebrated actors of his generation, Timothée Chalamet had a moment that nearly broke him. 

After seeing Interstellar for the first time at a cast screening in New York, Chalamet went home with his father and cried for nearly an hour.. realizing his role wasn’t as large as he had imagined. At the time, he believed the film might be a major breakthrough for him. Despite the disappointment, Chalamet later said he watched Interstellar twelve times in IMAX because he genuinely loved the film. He also revealed that while he filmed a long monologue, the scene ultimately stays focused on Matthew McConaughey’s face, quietly placing Chalamet’s performance in the background.

But instead of quitting, that disappointment became fuel. Today, Chalamet stands now at the very top of his generation. From Interstellar to Call Me by Your Name, Dune, Marty Supreme and upcoming dune 3, the journey makes one thing clear: small roles don’t limit you, they prepare you.

source_details.title: Interstellar
source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
